Okay, the most recent background task I kicked off was the comprehensive “glint” run that rebuilds the CLI with the new stall‑guard logic, injects a deliberately buggy `calc.py`, and asks the agent to iteratively fix the failing tests. That command is still executing in the background (ID be7wn3hwz). I can’t block waiting for it, but I do need to keep the overall debugging workflow moving forward.

What’s missing at this point? I’ve patched `agent.ts` to add an `emptyNudges` counter and corresponding guard, and I’ve reinforced the prompts in `prompts.ts` to emphasize never stopping midway. Those changes should improve the agent’s ability to handle empty replies and keep pushing forward, but I haven’t yet verified that the *subagent* delegation mechanism works correctly with the new code. The subagent tool is a core part of the “glint” architecture – it allows the main agent to spin up a secondary agent to perform a focused task, such as inspecting source files. Since I just introduced new guard logic that could affect turn handling, I need to make sure the subagent can still be invoked and can correctly read the list of tools from `src/core/tools.ts`.

The best way to test this is to run a small, isolated glint command that uses the `-p` (prompt) flag to ask the subagent tool to “investigate what tools are listed in /home/lane/GR/glint-cli/src/core/tools.ts (just names), then report the list.” I’ll run this in a clean temporary directory (`/tmp/glint-test`) to avoid any side‑effects from the earlier background job. I’ll also wrap the command in a `timeout` (240 seconds) so it won’t hang indefinitely, and I’ll pipe the output through `tail -8` to capture the final relevant lines (the subagent’s response). Running it with `bun run /home/lane/GR/glint-cli/src/index.tsx` mirrors how a user would invoke the CLI, and the `--yolo` flag keeps it from prompting for confirmation.

Because I still have the previous background task running, I’ll launch this subagent test as another background job. That way the system can continue processing both tasks concurrently, and I can later fetch the output of each via a `Read` call when needed.

Thus, the next step is to issue a Bash tool call that changes into `/tmp/glint-test`, runs the glint CLI with the appropriate prompt, and runs in the background. This will give me concrete evidence that the subagent delegation path works under the new stall‑guard changes.
